display.purpose: Page-level titles. One per page at most.

headline.purpose: Section headings and page headers — Heading.vue default and SectionShell titles.

title.purpose: Subsection headings inside a card or section.

body.purpose: All interface prose. The default size; descriptions cap around 65–75 characters.

label.purpose: Form labels, toolbar labels, chip text, row counts, helper text. Usually muted ink.

data.purpose: Machine-authored text only: log bodies, timestamps, ids, attribute pairs. Timestamps are tabular-nums.

shadows.name: state-lift
shadows.purpose: The hover/interactive whisper. Never applied at rest.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, dropdowns, popovers, sheets — elements that genuinely float above the page.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible state on every interactive element, paired with a border shift to --ring.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for every state transition.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and shadow transitions on buttons, chips, rows, and inputs.

motion.name: tail-pulse
motion.purpose: The live-tail radio icon while tailing is active — the only continuous motion in the product.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default action. Navy with cream text in light mode, gold with espresso text in dark.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--primary, hsl(215 51% 25%)); color: var(--primary-foreground, hsl(44 40% 95%)); font-family: 'Instrument Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25rem; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, hsl(215 51% 25%)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, hsl(215 51% 25%)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The secondary action. A hairline on the page ground that fills with the pale gold accent on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--border, hsl(42 18% 72%)); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--background, hsl(44 33% 93%)); color: var(--foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)); font-family: 'Instrument Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25rem; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--accent, hsl(45 74% 86%)); color: var(--accent-foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring, hsl(215 51% 25%)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, hsl(215 51% 25%)) 50%, transparent); }

components.description: No fill at rest, accent fill on hover. The default for icon-only controls in headers and rows.

components.name: Search Input
components.description: Transparent fill defined entirely by its darker field-edge stroke, with a leading 16px icon. Debounced; never paired with a submit button.
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position: relative; display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 360px; } .ds-input-icon { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 10px; transform: translateY(-50%); color: var(--muted-foreground, hsl(30 12% 40%)); pointer-events: none; } .ds-input-search { width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 4px 12px 4px 32px; border: 1px solid var(--input, hsl(42 18% 65%)); border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)); font-family: 'Instrument Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.25rem; outline: none; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input-search::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, hsl(30 12% 40%)); } .ds-input-search:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring, hsl(215 51% 25%)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, hsl(215 51% 25%)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-input-search[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--destructive, hsl(354 64% 51%)); }

components.name: Severity Chip
components.description: The signature control: the six-level filter row in the log toolbar. State is carried by fill, weight, and dot opacity together — never by colour alone.
components.css: .ds-severity-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .ds-severity-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border, hsl(42 18% 72%)); border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--background, hsl(44 33% 93%)); color: var(--muted-foreground, hsl(30 12% 40%)); font-family: 'Instrument Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1rem; text-transform: capitalize; cursor: pointer; outline: none; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-severity-chip .ds-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; opacity: 0.4; transition: opacity 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-severity-chip:hover { color: var(--foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)) 20%, transparent); } .ds-severity-chip:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, hsl(215 51% 25%)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-severity-chip.is-active { background: var(--secondary, hsl(43 28% 84%)); color: var(--secondary-foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)); font-weight: 600; border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)) 25%, transparent); } .ds-severity-chip.is-active .ds-dot { opacity: 1; }

components.name: Card
components.description: A warm near-white surface with a hairline and a 12px radius. Flat at rest — depth comes from the tonal ladder.
components.html:
Ingest endpoints

Point any OTLP-compatible exporter at your project key.

Rows appear in the viewer within a second of being queued.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 24px; padding: 24px 0; border: 1px solid var(--border, hsl(42 18% 72%)); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--card, hsl(44 50% 98%)); color: var(--card-foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)); font-family: 'Instrument Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card-header { display: grid; gap: 6px; padding: 0 24px; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.75rem; letter-spacing: -0.025em; } .ds-card-desc { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.25rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, hsl(30 12% 40%)); } .ds-card-content { padding: 0 24px; } .ds-card-body { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.25rem; }

components.name: Log Entry Row
components.description: The signature component. Fixed-width columns left of the message so the eye lands in the same place on every row; ruled by a bottom hairline, never stacked as cards.
components.css: .ds-log-list { width: 100%; } .ds-log-row { display: flex; width: 100%; align-items: flex-start; gap: 12px; padding: 6px 12px; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--sidebar-border, hsl(42 18% 72%)) 70%, transparent); background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, hsl(30 27% 17%)); font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1rem; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-log-row:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent, hsl(45 74% 86%)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-log-chevron { flex-shrink: 0; margin-top: 2px; color: var(--muted-foreground, hsl(30 12% 40%)); } .ds-log-time { flex-shrink: 0; color: var(--muted-foreground, hsl(30 12% 40%)); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-log-sev { display: inline-flex; flex-shrink: 0; align-items: center; gap: 6px; width: 64px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-log-sev .ds-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-log-service { flex-shrink: 0; width: 160px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--muted-foreground, hsl(30 12% 40%)); } .ds-log-body { flex: 1 1 0%; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }

components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; width: 220px; padding: 12px; background: var(--sidebar, hsl(44 26% 87%)); border-right: 1px solid var(--sidebar-border, hsl(42 18% 72%)); font-family: 'Instrument Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-nav-brand { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 4px 8px 12px; } .ds-nav-mark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--sidebar-primary, hsl(215 51% 25%)); color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground, hsl(44 40% 95%)); } .ds-nav-word { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25rem; color: var(--sidebar-foreground, hsl(30 20% 25%)); } .ds-nav-item { display: block; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--sidebar-foreground, hsl(30 20% 25%)); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25rem; text-decoration: none; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--sidebar-accent, hsl(43 26% 81%)); } .ds-nav-item.is-active { background: var(--sidebar-accent, hsl(43 26% 81%)); color: var(--sidebar-accent-foreground, hsl(30 27% 20%)); font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--sidebar-ring, hsl(215 51% 40%)) 50%, transparent); }

narrative.overview:
Bilis is a place built for long sessions with dense machine text. Somebody is going to sit in front of a log stream at two in the morning, scanning thousands of monospace lines for the one that explains the outage. Every decision in this system serves that person's eyes over that duration. Chrome recedes; content holds the contrast. The rhythm is generous where it costs nothing and tight where density earns its keep.

The character is utilitarian with a warm accent. Function comes first and says so — hairline borders, modest radii, no ornament that isn't doing work. The mid-century palette is the one concession to character, and it is spent deliberately: a cream page instead of a white one, espresso instead of black, navy and gold instead of a generic blue. That warmth is not decoration, it is ergonomics. Cream at 93% lightness and espresso ink at 17% is a gentler pairing to read for an hour than pure black on pure white, and the system's entire reason for choosing it is that the reading session is long.

Light and dark are two designed worlds, not one world with a filter over it. The primary voice actually changes between them — navy in light, gold in dark — and every severity colour is hand-tuned twice. Dark mode is where this product is most often used, and it is authored, not derived.
keyCharacteristics: Cream page, near-white surfaces, espresso ink — warm neutrals all the way down, never a pure white or a pure black.
A strict three-level surface ladder in light mode: page < card < hairline.
Colour is rationed. Severity is the only thing on screen allowed to be chromatic for its own sake.
Monospace is reserved for log data; the interface around it is Instrument Sans.
Flat at rest. Depth is a response to state, not a resting property.
Every reusable component appears in /styleguide. A component that isn't there isn't done.

rules.name: The Two Primaries Rule
rules.body: Navy is the light-mode voice; gold is the dark-mode voice. Both are first-class and neither is derived from the other. Always reference --primary / bg-primary; never hardcode either hex, and never assume the primary is dark — in dark mode it is the brightest thing on screen and requires --primary-foreground (espresso) on top of it.

rules.name: The Reserved Ramp Rule
rules.body: The six severity colours mean severity and nothing else. No badge, chart series, chip, illustration, or decorative accent may borrow a severity value for a non-severity meaning. When a UI needs a colour and it isn't communicating log severity, it takes one from the semantic tokens or the brand stripes.

rules.name: The No Pure Values Rule
rules.body: No #fff, no #000, no neutral grey with zero chroma anywhere in the interface. Every neutral carries warmth. A cool grey next to cream reads as a mistake.

rules.name: The Twice-Tuned Rule
rules.body: Every colour that appears in both modes is authored twice. Never derive a dark-mode value by fading, lightening, or applying opacity to its light-mode counterpart.

rules.name: The Monospace Boundary Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks machine-authored text. Log bodies, timestamps, ids, and attribute pairs are monospace; every label about them drops back to Instrument Sans. The typeface change is how a reader tells the record from the annotation.

rules.name: The 14/12 Rule
rules.body: Interface copy is 14px and support copy is 12px. There is no 16px body and no 13px anything. Two sizes carry ninety percent of the product, which is what lets a dense table and its surrounding chrome share one rhythm.

rules.name: The Tabular Timestamp Rule
rules.body: Any column of numbers a reader scans vertically — timestamps above all — is tabular-nums. Digits that shift width break the scan.

rules.name: The Surface Declaration Rule
rules.body: A rounded-xl border alone sits at page level and disappears. Any element that should read as a surface must declare bg-card. This is the practical consequence of the three-level ladder and it is the single most common way to break light mode.

rules.name: The Fixed Column Rule
rules.body: In the log stream, every column left of the message has a fixed width. Nothing shifts between rows.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: If an element's state has not changed, it casts no shadow. Structure is carried by tone and hairline. A shadow on a resting card is borrowed depth the ladder already provides.

rules.name: The Hairline-Only Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px. To emphasise an element, change its fill or its tone; never thicken its stroke.

dos: Do give every panel that should read as a surface bg-card. A bordered box without it sits at page level and vanishes.
Do reference semantic tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, border-border) in components. Raw brand utilities (bg-navy, text-gold) are for deliberate brand moments only.
Do author every colour twice — a hand-tuned light value and a hand-tuned dark value.
Do pair severity colour with the dot and the uppercase text label. Colour never carries severity by itself.
Do use tabular-nums on any column of digits a reader scans vertically.
Do keep monospace for machine-authored text and Instrument Sans for everything the interface says about it.
Do add every new reusable component to /styleguide in the same change, with realistic Bilis-flavoured demo content.
Do keep borders at 1px and create emphasis with fill or tone.
donts: Don't use #fff, #000, or a zero-chroma grey. Every neutral in this system is warm.
Don't borrow a severity colour for anything that isn't log severity.
Don't assume the primary is dark — in dark mode it is gold, and it needs espresso text on top of it.
Don't derive a dark-mode value by fading or lightening its light-mode counterpart.
Don't put a resting shadow on a surface. Shadow is a response to hover, focus, or floating.
Don't let column widths vary between log rows, or the vertical scan breaks.
Don't introduce a third interface type size. 14px body and 12px support carry the product.
Don't hardcode a chart colour or import from 'echarts' — go through lib/echarts.ts and useChartTokens().
Don't add a second page header. The breadcrumb bar is the page's identity.
